_note: The guided intro, in order, played in the 1900 scenario. title and text are what the card says. highlight names the real control to outline: {button: text of a button}, {group: a node group} (a window, the top bar, the map mode bar), or none. done is what completes the step: {command: class name}, {signal: camera | province_selected | mode_changed | game_saved}, {mode: [map modes]}, {window: group of a window that must be open} or {ack: true} (the Got it button). requires: fleet skips the step for a nation with no fleet. Every step can be skipped.

steps.title: Move around the map
steps.text: Hold W, A, S and D to pan, or drag with the middle mouse button. Turn the wheel to zoom in and out. The year is 1900: Europe is at peace, and what happens next is up to you and the other powers.

steps.title: Select a province
steps.text: Click any province. The card at the top left tells you who owns it and what is there; More shows the rest.

steps.title: Read a map mode
steps.text: The buttons at the bottom left recolour the map: who owns what, alliances, the economy, population, armies, terrain. Click one (keys 1 to 6 do the same).

steps.title: Open the Nation screen
steps.text: Everything about running your country is one window with a tab for each part: Overview, Economy, Build, Military, Navy, Diplomacy, Focus and Rankings. The Overview lists what needs your attention. Click Nation (or press N).

steps.title: Read the budget
steps.text: On the Economy tab (E) the Gold section shows what comes in each month (your provinces' base income, civilian factories and ports) and what goes out (the army, the navy, the buildings' upkeep). Construction shows your construction points. Under People, set the standing army: every division costs upkeep each month, so a nation that expects war keeps a larger one.

steps.title: Build something
steps.text: On the Build tab (B) pick a building, then click a green province on the map. A building costs gold and construction points, paid when it starts, and is finished after its days; a civilian factory earns gold every month. The queue at the bottom right shows progress.

steps.title: Raise an army
steps.text: On the Military tab (M), pick one of your provinces on the map, open Recruit and raise a unit. Units cost gold and recruits, then upkeep every month, and form an army where they were raised.

steps.title: Move an army
steps.text: Click an army to select it, then right-click a province to send it there. Drag a box to select several at once. Press Space to start the clock, and armies will march.

steps.title: Set a front
steps.text: Press C to open the command panel. It holds your armies as cards and every order for them. Draw a front: a line of provinces your army holds against a neighbour. Armies assigned to a front defend it.

steps.title: Improve relations
steps.text: On the Diplomacy tab (F) choose a nation and improve relations with it. Diplomatic effort costs diplomacy points, shown in the top bar. Alliances, guarantees and war all start here.

steps.title: Make a demand
steps.text: Also on the Diplomacy tab: Make a demand. Choose what you ask of a nation (provinces, or a concession such as reparations) and it has weeks to answer. If it refuses, you hold a casus belli with that demand as the goal of the war. Try one on a weak neighbour, for a small concession.

steps.title: Choose a national focus
steps.text: On the Focus tab (O) start a focus: a few weeks of national effort that grows the economy, enlarges the army or earns prestige and claims. One at a time; the tree shows what each needs.

steps.title: Watch Europe's tension
steps.text: The flame in the top bar is Europe's tension, from 0 to 100. It rises with the arms race, mobilization and rivalry, and with crises like those of 1905, 1908 and 1911. When a crisis concerns you, time stops and you choose how to answer. The higher it gets, the bolder the other powers become. Nothing says the war must come.

steps.title: How a war ends
steps.text: In a war, battles and the ground you hold earn war score. At peace you pay for what you take in score, and your war's goal costs half; land must touch your own. A nation whose people will not fight on, or that has lost most of its ground, gives more. The peace screen (Diplomacy tab, at war) shows it all.

steps.title: Send a fleet
steps.text: On the Navy tab (Y) select a fleet, then right-click a patch of sea to send it there. Fleets in the right waters can cut an enemy's trade. New ships are built at your ports from the same daily building capacity as buildings.

steps.title: Save your game
steps.text: Press F5 to quick save, or F6 for the save window; Esc opens the menu, which also lists every key. The game saves itself on the first of every month. Good luck.
